UPDATE: JAGERSFONTEIN

By: Matuba Mahlatjie | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Looking back at three years since the damn collapse.

Unique Selling Point:
There's now a civil case as well as a criminal case to hold people accountable for the loss of life and livellihood since the incident.

Summary:
"The mine officials, as well as consultants who do the social and Labour government as well as the environmental impact assessments report, are brought to court to account on a criminal level in so far as having caused the deaths that took place in as well as causing damage to people's properties, as well as the properties of the municipality. So, until the end of the criminal hearings is finalised, there will not be true justice in Jaggersfontein."

Script:


VO
It was a disaster that claimed five lives, wiped out homes, and left a community buried in sludge. A TAILINGS DAM AT A FREE STATE MINING OPERATION COLLAPSED, AND OVER 6 MILLION CUBIC METERS OF CONTAMINATED WASTE FLOODED THE AREA.
[pause] [Date on screen: 11 September 2022]
For three years, the people of Jagersfontein have waited for one thing: justice.

VO
NOW, five individuals and three companies, FACE 13 CHARGES, INCLUDING THREE COUNTS OF MURDER. THE ACCUSED APPEARED IN COURT BRIEFLY EARLIER THIS MONTH.
[GRAPHIC: Text on screen: "5 INDIVIDUALS AND 3 COMPANIES CHARGED WITH MURDER]

UPSOUND/Andries Nkome/Lawyer
"The mine officials, as well as consultants that do up the social and Labour government as well as the environmental impact assessments report are brought to court to account on a criminal level in so far as having caused the deaths that took place in as well as causing damage to people's properties, as well as the properties of the municipality. So we are saying, up until such time as the end of the criminal hearings have been finalised, there will not really be justice in Jagersfontein."

VO
While the state pursues criminal charges, a parallel civil battle for financial compensation is being waged on behalf of the victims. Representing residents, ATTORNEY Andries Nkome, says it's not just about destroyed property, but also the loss of livelihoods and the contamination of the environment.

UPSOUND/Andries Nkome/Lawyer
We have named as defendants the owners of the mine development. We've also sued the Department of Mineral Resources as well as the Department of Water and Sanitation that ministers thereof.

VO
The criminal case echoes the warnings experts and residents gave for years, and which we revealed in our original broadcast.

UPSOUND/Archival soundbite: Dr. Charles MacRobert
“So tailings dams are inanimate. They don't make decisions to fail. And so so people take decisions within a knowledge base to prevent failure.”

UPSOUND/Archival soundbite Lindile Saula from original report.
“We told them that the dam is not safe. We told the managers of the mines for 4 to 5 years.”

VO
While about 90 families opted to have their houses rebuilt instead of a civil case, the environmental damage and the human trauma are scars that may never fully heal.

UPSOUND/Andries Nkome/Lawyer
There are those whose properties are now damaged again, so therefore they got essentially nowhere to run. We are. We have been saying to them that they ought to come and be part of the litigation, simply because, with a court order or a settlement agreement that is made, you are able to be put back in the position where, prior to the demo collapse. So it's only so sad that they find themselves in the position…
